newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's top groups to freeze executive pay.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's top groups to freeze executive pay.

text.p: South Korea's top business groups agreed on Tuesday to freeze total spending on executive pay and benefits next year, an official of the Federation of Korean Industries said.

The decision was made after a meeting of heads of 30 industrial conglomerates, known as chaebol, the official told a news conference. The meeting had been expected to endorse a freeze on wage spending across the board, and cuts in the workforce.
"They agreed today to freeze total spending on wages and benefits for executives of 30 top groups," Chun Dae-joo said, referring to the chaebol heads, including the chairmen of the
For workers below the executive level, the chaebol will follow guidelines set out by the Korea Employers' Federation, Chun said.
The federation recommends pay increases taking into account the wishes of the government, unions and employers.
An earlier meeting of chaebol planning heads advised a freeze on total staff pay and early retirement schemes.
The earlier proposal drew fire from the nation's powerful unions.

It now appears the chaebol have backed down from a strategy that almost certainly would have led to industrial confrontation. Korean workers are virtually guaranteed a job for life and layoffs are almost unheard of.
"To overcome economic difficulties, they agreed to restructure their businesses aggressively and streamline their organisations and cut their expenditure on entertaining," Chun told reporters.
"Wage freezes are not just for the benefit of the companies. They are a token of our efforts to step into the ranks of advanced countries," Chun said.

He said the chaebol chairmen would urge the government to lower interest rates to help businesses. South Korean rates are among the highest in the world and many businesses are now squeezed for cash as a result.
Corporate profits have been savaged this year by a weak Japanese yen and plunging prices for key exports, most notably semiconductors.
